extracted.intended_audience: individuals and organizations who want to submit public comments on federal regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and submitting effective public comments on proposed federal regulations, including procedural requirements, comment structure, and persuasive strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can comment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone may submit a comment — individuals, community groups, trade associations, NGOs, companies, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to comment on
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed federal regulations during designated comment periods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address the text, rationale, or impacts of a proposed rule; focus on the specific regulatory proposal under review.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: During the official comment window (typically 30-60 days)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit within the published comment period for the notice of proposed rulemaking; late comments may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the agency's designated submission portal (most commonly regulations.gov) and follow its instructions for uploading or entering comment text and attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — Introduction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin the comment by making your stance (support, oppose, or conditionally support) unmistakable; a clear opening helps reviewers quickly understand your perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — Body
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evidence, analysis, and supporting details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The body should contain factual evidence, reasoning, citations, and examples that explain why the agency should accept or reject the proposal or adopt revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — Conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize your stance and desired outcome
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End with a concise summary of your position and explicitly state the changes or outcome you seek from the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the proposed rule carefully; understand the agency's stated rationale; identify specific regulatory language being challenged
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before drafting, analyze the rule text and preamble, note the agency's reasons and data, and pinpoint exact provisions you address so your comment targets concrete language rather than generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take a stance
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether you support, oppose, or conditionally support the regulation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your position unmistakably clear from the beginning; if conditional, specify the conditions under which you would support the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference exact regulatory sections and page numbers; cite specific provisions rather than speaking in generalities; provide concrete examples demonstrating impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise citations (e.g., section numbers, docket citations, page/line references) and concrete examples or data showing how the rule would affect people, organizations, or practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer alternative options
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose specific modifications or revisions; suggest workable solutions to identified problems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do more than criticize: recommend concrete edits (language changes, different compliance timelines, exemptions, metrics) and explain why those alternatives fix the problem and are administratively feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the 'other side'
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge counterarguments; respond substantively to opposing viewpoints; show you've considered multiple perspectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate likely agency or stakeholder objections, briefly concede valid points where appropriate, and rebut or accommodate contrary positions with evidence or compromise proposals to strengthen credibility.
